concept_weaknesses: The concept proposes expansion to a third school, but the listed evidence confirms MOUs with only two New Haven schools; a partnership or commitment from the third school is not documented.
The outcomes need clearer measurement details, including how a DIBELS benchmark-level gain will be defined and what student and family participation counts as the denominator.
The concept should explain how 40 tutors will be recruited, trained, supervised, and matched with 120 students.
unsupported_claims: “Our tutoring model produced gains for most students in 2025” is not substantiated by the listed evidence, which reports that 241 students received pre/post assessments but provides no results.
“Our program is proven to double reading growth” is not supported by the listed evidence.
The claim that fewer than half of K-3 students at partner schools read at grade level relies on school-reported data not included among the listed evidence assets.
concerns: The foundation states that it does not accept unsolicited proposals, so the organization should not submit this concept without an invitation.
The proposed scale and activities may require more staff time than the listed 30 staff-capacity hours per month; feasibility should be confirmed.
rationale: The foundation makes grants by invitation only and explicitly rejects unsolicited proposals. Its stated interest in early childhood literacy in Connecticut aligns with the organization’s mission and geography, but there is no formal application path or invitation identified. Build a relationship and confirm whether an invitation is possible before preparing or submitting a proposal.
